summary: Over a 14-day evaluation period, the user achieved an 86.0% time-in-range (70-180 mg/dL), with 8.9% time above range and 5.1% time below range. The data demonstrates a heavy reliance on automated UAM (Unannounced Meals) and SMBs, with zero recorded manual carbohydrate entries. While overall glycemic stability is good, nighttime hours (00:00-04:00) show elevated hypoglycemia risk (up to 18.5% below 70 mg/dL), and afternoon/evening hours show predictable postprandial hyperglycemia peaks due to the absence of meal announcements or preboluses.

analysis_steps.evidence: 3,995 valid CGM entries over 14 days (98.7% coverage, stable ~5-minute cadence). 2,315 total treatments including 655 insulin entries (275.95 U total) and 0 carbohydrate entries.
analysis_steps.findings: Data quality is good. CGM and telemetry continuity are excellent. The complete absence of logged carbohydrate entries indicates full reliance on UAM, SMB, and manual corrections.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of meal carbohydrate data limits direct evaluation of Carb Ratios via standard postprandial excursions.

analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%. Glucose extremes show lows reaching 41-54 mg/dL primarily overnight (01:00-04:00) and late afternoon (17:00). Afternoon peaks reach up to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.findings: Nighttime and late-afternoon hypoglycemia periods require attention. Afternoon glycemic excursions reflect unannounced meal impacts managed solely by loop automation.

analysis_steps.evidence: Local hourly glucose averages are 90-106 mg/dL overnight, but 10.1% to 18.5% time below range occurs between 00:00 and 03:00. Basal rates range from 0.5 to 0.8 U/h.
analysis_steps.findings: Current early-night basal rates (00:00 at 0.6 U/h and 05:00 at 0.7 U/h) deliver excessive insulin during early sleep, causing frequent dips below 70 mg/dL.

analysis_steps.evidence: ISF is configured as a single flat segment of 56 mg/dL/U. CR segments span 5 blocks (10.5 to 13.2 g/U). DIA is set to 10 hours.
analysis_steps.findings: A single flat ISF across 24 hours is overly broad, though AAPS dynamic sensitivity (at 70%) actively compensates in real-time. Lack of carb entries prevents direct CR validation.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No declared carbohydrate or meal bolus data to validate CR segments.

analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_always_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3 min, max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min, max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min.
analysis_steps.findings: Automation settings are correctly optimized for an unannounced meal workflow. SMB and UAM are active and appropriately pacing microboluses in response to rising glucose deltas.

analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true (70% adjustment factor), max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h, max_iob_units=25 U.
analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic sensitivity is active and compressing ISF during highs. Max IOB of 25 U is high relative to total daily insulin (~20 U/day) and presents a safety consideration for insulin stacking.

analysis_steps.evidence: Treatment summary shows 0 carb entries and therapy response windows contain only automated corrections and microboluses.
analysis_steps.findings: The user relies entirely on UAM and automated SMBs without prebolusing or meal announcements, resulting in postprandial afternoon peaks before loop automation catches up.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of declared meal or carb data.

analysis_steps.evidence: Extended carb entries and e-carb treatments equal 0. Absorption modeling relies on UAM settings (meal_max_absorption_hours=7 h).
analysis_steps.findings: Extended carbs and empirical e-carb absorption profiles are not utilized; all postprandial absorption is handled by UAM.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No e-carb or extended absorption usage.

analysis_steps.evidence: Combined evaluation of good data quality, nighttime hypoglycemia patterns, afternoon postprandial peaks, and UAM-dependent automation.
analysis_steps.findings: Prioritize resolving early-night hypoglycemia by adjusting the 00:00 basal segment. Maintain automation settings and address meal strategy via observation.

strengths: High CGM time-in-range of 86.0% over the 14-day evaluation period.
Robust data continuity (98.7% CGM coverage) and stable cadence.
Well-configured closed-loop automation (SMB and UAM enabled with appropriate pacing intervals) successfully managing unannounced meals.
issues: Elevated time below range (10.1% to 18.5% below 70 mg/dL) during early night hours (00:00-03:00).
Afternoon and evening postprandial hyperglycemia peaks (hourly averages up to 162.8 mg/dL) due to pure UAM reliance without preboluses.
Single flat ISF profile (56 mg/dL/U) across all hours, relying heavily on dynamic sensitivity adjustments.

recommendations.title: Reduce Early-Night Basal Rate
recommendations.description: Telemetry shows frequent hypoglycemia between 00:00 and 03:00 local time, indicating excess basal insulin delivery during the early night.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Early-night hypoglycemia (10.1% to 18.5% time below range between 00:00 and 03:00) indicates that the 00:00 basal rate of 0.6 U/h delivers slightly too much insulin during early sleep.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight glucose for at least 5 consecutive nights after adjusting the 00:00 basal segment to 0.5 U/h to confirm elimination of early-night dips below 70 mg/dL.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Lower the 00:00 basal rate from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h while keeping all other basal, CR, ISF, target, and DIA settings unchanged.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Maintain current automated UAM and SMB workflow while observing postprandial responses. Consider logging carbohydrate entries for select meals to evaluate whether pre-meal announcements and prebolusing improve postprandial time-in-range.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: In the absence of manual carbohydrate entries and preboluses, the closed-loop system relies entirely on UAM detection and dynamic ISF compression to manage meals. While achieving an 86% TIR, this approach results in predictable afternoon postprandial hyperglycemia peaks before the loop catches up.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record carbohydrate entries and pre-meal boluses for at least three consecutive meals to assess impact on postprandial glucose excursions.

implementation_steps: Verify current basal and loop settings with the care team before making changes.
Implement the single basal adjustment (lowering profile.basal.00_00 from 0.6 U/h to 0.5 U/h) while keeping all other profile and automation settings unchanged.
Monitor overnight CGM trends closely for 5 consecutive nights to confirm reduction of early-night hypoglycemia.
Evaluate postprandial glucose patterns after overnight stability is established before considering any further parameter adjustments.
education: Closed-loop automation (SMB and UAM) relies on positive glucose deltas to deliver microboluses when meals are unannounced, which can lead to temporary postprandial rises before insulin action takes effect.
Adjusting basal rates requires patience; changes should be made sequentially and evaluated over several days while keeping other settings constant.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
